Subject: Scheduled rolling restart: EastUS2 node reboots (June 21-22 UTC)

Hi all,

Heads-up from Infra: we have a scheduled, rolling node restart in the EastUS2 region to apply a kernel/driver update that reduces kernel-CPU contention under certain AVX workloads. This is a planned maintenance window across dedicated and hosted pools in eastus2.

Planned window:
- Start: 2026-06-21 23:00 UTC
- End: 2026-06-22 07:00 UTC
- Pattern: zone-by-zone rolling restarts (one AZ at a time); each node reboot is expected to take ~2-4 minutes plus ~3-5 minutes for post-start health checks.

Expected impact:
- Short, infrequent latency spikes for in-flight requests during individual node restarts.
- No cluster-wide outage expected; traffic will be drained and routed to healthy nodes.
- Bulk ingestion jobs running at the exact minute of a node reboot may see a transient retry/failure depending on client retry logic.

What we need from you:
- If you or your customers have critical jobs that cannot tolerate a 10-minute window within the above period, reply with the job name and target time and we will coordinate a brief exclusion or schedule adjustment.
- Please review the attached maintenance plan and the runbook link below.

Attachments: maintenance-plan-eastus2.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
Runbook: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/eastus2-reboot
Status: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2026-06-21-eastus2

We will post live updates on the status page during the window and alert on PagerDuty for any unexpected regressions.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

--
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jun 15, 2026 at 18:03 Platform Ops <platform-ops@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads-up, Hannah. Quick question: our nightly bulk ingestion window runs 2026-06-22 02:00-03:00 UTC and we have ~30 concurrent writers that open long-lived TCP connections to your hosted endpoints. Are those connections likely to be terminated mid-job, or will the connection be drained gracefully and retried by your load balancers?

Hi Jacob — Laura here from Prod SRE. Short answer: connections are drained per-node before reboot; in practice this looks like a graceful close with an HTTP 429/502 on a small percentage of long polls depending on client timeout/keepalive. The rolling pattern means we will not reboot multiple nodes within the same AZ simultaneously and we keep at least 30% spare capacity to accept traffic.

More detail:
- Drain + reboot per node: we first mark node as DRAINING in routing, wait up to 60s for in-flight requests to finish, then trigger kernel patch + reboot.
- Typical per-node impact: 2–4 minutes for reboot, plus 3–5 minutes for health-probe-based warm-up; from a client perspective ~1–2 failed requests per 10k requests in the busiest pools is a reasonable worst-case for the window.
- Bulk ingestion guidance: we recommend either shifting Acme's ingestion window outside the 23:00–07:00 UTC window, or adding idempotent retries with exponential backoff (2xx retry) for the 02:00 job to tolerate up to a 2–3 minute transient.

If you need, we can coordinate a 1-hour exclusion for Acme's tenant; Marcus, Rafael — can you confirm whether an exclusion is feasible and if we need to run a special-drain to move traffic off all nodes serving Acme?

Attachment: node-reboot-runbook.md (Markdown, 8KB)

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Jacob — thanks for the question and the quick follow-up.

We can offer Acme a 1-hour exclusion from 02:00–03:00 UTC on 2026-06-22. That will require us to temporarily pin their tenant traffic to a protected pool for that hour; Marcus and Rafael, can you confirm capacity to accept the pinned traffic? If yes, we'll update the maintenance page and send a final confirmation by EOD 2026-06-17.

If Acme prefers to keep the slot as-is, please implement the recommended retry behavior (idempotent retries with jitter) — Laura's runbook has the exact probe/timeout values.

I'll update the status link once the exclusion is set.

Thanks — Hannah
